name: Continuous Polynomial Discretization
description: Hides the discrete {1,2,3} search space behind a rational fixed-point equation whose only real roots are 1, 2, and 3. Hides the inequality constraint (u != v) behind a continuous rational inequality (x/y + y/x > 2). This prevents models from immediately recognizing the problem as discrete graph coloring, causing pattern-matching models to attempt continuous optimization or fail to implement the necessary backtracking search.
